title: How To Handle Students Who Complain
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers teachers a five-step response to student complaining—smile, remember, empathize, explain, smile—designed to defuse frustration without creating friction. He counsels pausing before reacting, recognizing complaining as a normal part of childhood rather than a sign of teaching failure, and genuinely empathizing since every teacher was once a frustrated student themselves. He recommends briefly explaining the reasoning behind an assignment, citing research on the persuasive power of the word 'because,' before closing warmly. He frames occasional discomfort and complaint as a healthy sign that students are being appropriately challenged, arguing that a teacher's calm empathy, not defensiveness, is what ultimately helps students push through resistance and embrace difficulty.
points: Offers a five-step response—smile, remember, empathize, explain, smile—for defusing student complaints without friction.
Reframes occasional student complaining as a normal, even healthy, sign that students are being appropriately challenged.
Cites research on the persuasive power of the word 'because' when briefly explaining an assignment's purpose.
Advises genuine empathy, recalling one's own experience as a frustrated student, rather than defensiveness.
Argues teacher empathy, not argument, is what ultimately helps students push through discomfort and embrace difficulty.
quotes: It can take willpower not to reply with a sharp, “Because I said so” or “So sad, too bad.” It can be hard not to glare, fume, and hold a private grudge.
It helps to remember that they’re just kids, and complaining is part of growing up. It’s in their DNA, and okay.
Sometimes a genuine smile is all you need. But if they persist, tell them that you understand—because you do.

Students get irritated when they don’t know why you’re doing what you’re doing. So tell them. Be transparent. Studies show that when you use the word ‘because’ you’ll experience greater influence and buy-in, even if the reason is nonsensical.
The key to getting them through those tough moments is your empathy and unwillingness to take their complaining personally.
They set aside their compulsion to complain and avoid difficulty, and instead embrace it as part of the pursuit of excellence you live and breathe and pursue every day.
